category_title: Students with EBD who are frequently off-task and disruptive during independent seatwork
minimal_context: The student is copying new vocabulary definitions into their notebook during reading instruction in a general education classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please copy these new vocabulary definitions from the dictionary into your notebook.

STUDENT: I don't get this. The definition has words I don't even know. This is confusing.

TUTOR: Just do your best to read it and write it down.

STUDENT: (Puts pencil down and pushes the notebook away) No, I'm not copying all this.

TUTOR: You need to finish your vocabulary assignment.

STUDENT: (Turns around to the desk behind them and grabs their classmate's paper) Hey, stop working and look at what I'm doing. This is boring anyway.

options.A: Withhold attention from the student when they engage in the disruptive behavior during the vocabulary assignment.
options.B: Provide multiple meaningful opportunities to work with the new vocabulary words through discussion, writing, and reading.
options.C: Terminate the instructional demands and remove the vocabulary materials from the student's desk for 10 seconds.
options.D: Lower expectations for the student and reduce the assignment, asking them to copy fewer vocabulary definitions.
